description_en: Cikã Bahī, located in Cyāsal Ṭola, used to be one of the largest and most activebahīs. It sits on a relatively high-up parcel of land which can be accessed via a flight of stone steps. Thebahīis surrounded by two-story high buildings. The main entrance is located in the east; stepping through this, one finds oneself in a colonnaded portico with a statue of Māhāṅkal. The main sanctum is aligned with this main entrance. A spire (pucā)on the hip roof indicates the location of the main deity below. Acaityashaped pinnacle has been placed on top of thepucā,and on top of the pinnacle one can find anāgachatra.The monastic building has undergone many reconstructions over the past decades and today the sanctum is the only part of original structure. The reconstructions were financed through donations from local donors and grants from the municipality. However, financial issues have also prevented this work from being fully completed.The monastic building was initially planned to be a centre for education, and must have had a colonnaded ground floor. The west and east wings both boast nine bays of colonnades, while the north and south wings seem to have been built to be roomy and spacious. An open balcony runs all along the first floor, though the section that passes through the main shrine is closed off somewhat by slanting windows (gā jhyā) and is topped with apucā. The slanting window section is supported by a pair of timber posts that rise up from the ground floor.In the courtyard, there are three votivecaityas, images of the donors, and adharmadhātu. The courtyard floor is paved with telia tiles and the original plinths have been retained on the east and west, raised 56cm from the lower level. Large bricks have been used instead of stone to edge the plinth in the east wing. In front of the main sanctum, the plinth protrudes outwards somewhat; this section is made with a stone floor and stone edging. The monastery wall were rebuilt using limesurkhimortar, and the thickness of the wall was reduced to 35cm. New lattice windows and doors are of inferior quality.Images ofaṣṭamaṅgalasare engraved on the main doors' panels and small statues of the Five Buddhas are afixed to the wall above the entrance.The entrance to the sanctum has been decorated with various objects, and is flanked by two lion statues. On the outer sides of the statues are two bells hanging on the stone beams, behind which one can see two bronze flags. Paintings of Sāriputra and Maudagalyayana can be found on either side of the entrance, and two rows of threemānesare present on the outer sides of each of these paintings. Above the left-hand sidemāne,one can find a painting of an unidentified creature with ten heads; nine are human-like, while the tenth is in the shape of a horse. Similarly, themāneon the right is also underneath a painting of an unidentified creature with one human head and one bird's head attached to it. Stone inscriptions have been placed in a row on the plinth. The door is clad in bronze, and above it one can find atoraṇadepicting the Five Buddhas, Akṣobhya Buddha, and Prajñāpāramitā and Ṣaḍakṣarī Lokeśvara. Images of the Five Buddhas can also be found on the wall behind thetoraṇa.Inside the sanctum, there is a metal image of Akṣobhya Buddha performing the gesture ofbhūsparśa. His body is covered by his metal attire (hegā). Behind the image, one can find a metaltoraṇain the form of creepers and flowers. Thetoraṇais flanked by images of Sāriputra and Maudgalyāyana, although these are replicas; the original images were stolen. In addition to these images, one can also find several other small images of Buddha inside the sanctum. Anāgãdyaḥis located on the top floor of thedyaḥchẽand, according to thesaṅghamembers of the Bahī, this room contains a metal image of Vārāhī.The classical Sanskrit name of the Bahī is Saptapura Mahāvihāra. In the inscriptions of the Malla period this Bahī is called Cupiṃkhā Vihāra, Cilaṃ Vihāra or Cupiri Vihāra. Its modern name, Cikã Bahī, seems to be derived from these words. In an inscription dated NS 144 (1024 CE) placed inside the Guitaḥ Bahī (Prathamapura Mahāvihāra) of Patan, this Bahī is referred to as Gautamaśrī Saṃskārita Bahī. As such, it can be alleged that this Bahī was established before this date by someone called Gautamaśrī. The other five branches of thisvihāra- which in fact has the most branchvihārasof all - are Maṇikula, Triratna, Bhaiṣajyarāja and Sumaṅgala Vihāra of Patan, as well as onevihāralocated in Koteshwor Kathmandu.According toLocke(1985, 212), the Cikã Bahīhad 135saṅghamembers in 1985 making it the largest and most activesaṅghaof all thebahīsin Patan. Only initated Śākyas can be members of thesaṅgha. The lineage deity is Vajravārāhī, who is located at her shrine near Chapagaun (to the south of Patan). Thesaṅghaperforms the daily ritual worship and other religious social activities. The duty of worship is handed over once a week on Sunday from one family to another, and the family on active duty sleeps inside the Bahī complex until the next hand-over. Theguṭhīlands endowed for the Bahī have been sold or given up, meaning that many rituals are now endangered. Nowadays, these activities are continued with the help of donations collected by thesaṅghamembers
description_ne: चिकँ बही च्यासल टोलमा च्यासल हिटीबाट करिब ३० मी. दुरीमा पश्चिमपट्टि अवस्थित छ । बही प्रवेश गर्ने काठको मूलढोका बही परिसरको पूर्वी भवनमा रहेको छ । ढोकाको खापामा अष्टमङ्गल कुँदिएको छ र ढोकामाथि गाह्रोमा पञ्चबुद्धको स-साना प्रतिमा राखिएको छ । ढोकाबाट भित्र पस्दै गर्दा दायाँतिर भित्तामा रहेको प्रतिमास्थानमा महाकालको प्रतिमा देख्न सकिन्छ । चतुष्कोणाकार बहीचोकको वरिपरि चारै तिर दुईतले भवन रहेको छ र माथिल्लो तलामा रिङ्गै बार्दली रहेको छ भने पश्चिमपट्टि रहेको भवनमा गा झ्याल रहेको छ। पश्चिमपट्टि रहेको भवनको भुईँ तलामा द्यःछेँ रहेको छ । सो भवनको छानाको बीचमा पुर निर्माण गरी त्यसमाथि चैत्याकार गजूर राखिएको छ अनि गजूरमाथि नागछत्र ओढाइएको छ । गर्भगृह प्रवेश गर्ने ढोका र ढोकाको आसपास विशेष साजसज्जा देखिन्छ । ढोकासम्म पुग्ने खुड्किलाको दायाँ-बायाँ सिंहका प्रतिमा छन् र ती प्रतिमाका नजिकै बाहिरपट्टि दुईवटा घण्टा झुण्ड्याइएका छन् । दुबै सिंहका प्रतिमाभन्दा पछाडि पित्तलका झण्डा खडा गरिएका छन् ।  ढोकाको दायाँ-बायाँ भित्तामा सारिपुत्र र मौद्गल्यानको चित्र कोरिएको छ । दुवै चित्रको माथिपट्टि तीन-तीन वटा मानेका दुई लहर राखिएका छन् । पेटीमा लहरै शिलालेखहरू ठड्याइएका छन् ।  ढोकालाई पित्तलले मोडिएको छ र ढोकामाथि तामाको तोरण रहेको छ । तोरणमा माथि पञ्चबुद्धका प्रतिमाहरू छन् भने तल प्रज्ञापारमिता र षडक्षरी लोकेश्वरको बीचमा अक्षोभ्य बुद्धको प्रतिमा छ । तोरणभन्दा पछाडिको भित्तामा पञ्चबुद्धका चित्रहरू लहरै कोरिएका छन् ।द्यःछेँको गर्भगृहमा बाहाको प्रमुख देवताको रूपमा भूस्पर्श मुद्रामा अक्षोभ्य बुद्धको धातुको प्रतिमा रहेको छ । अक्ष्योभ्यलाई धातुको बुट्टेदार  हेगा ओढाइएको छ । मूर्ति पछाडि पुष्प र पत्र भएको धातुकै तोरण छ र दायाँ-बायाँ सारिपुत्र र मौद्गल्यायनको प्रतिमा राखिएको छ । पुरानो मूर्ति चोरी भएकोले त्यसकै प्रतिरूप नयाँ मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको हो । गर्भगृहमा मुख्य मूर्तिको अलावा बुद्धका अन्य स-साना मूर्तिहरू पनि रहेका छन् । द्यःछेँको माथिल्लो तलामा सम्बन्धित संघको आगंद्यः राखिएको छ । संघका सदस्यका अनुसार आगंद्यःको रूपमा गुह्यकक्षभित्र वाराहीको धातुमूर्ति स्थापित छ ।यस चिकं बहीको संस्कृत नाम ''सप्तपुर महाविहार'' हो । मल्लकालीन अभिलखहरूमा यस विहारको ''चुपिंखा विहार'', ''चिलं विहार'' अथवा ''चुपिरि विहार'' नाम रहेको पाइन्छ र तिनै शब्दको अपभ्रंश रूप नै आजभोलिको ''चिकंविही'' नाम हो भन्ने स्पष्ट हुन्छ । पाटनको गुइतःबही (प्रथमपुर महाविहार) मा रहेको नेसं १४४ को अभिलेखमा यस बहीको नामोल्लेख भएबाट यो बही त्यस मितिभन्दा अघि नै निर्माण भैसकेको तथ्य ज्ञात हुन्छ । सोही अभिलेखमा यस बहीलाई ''गौतमश्री संस्कारित'' भनिएबाट यसको निर्माण गौतमश्रीद्वारा गरिएको हो भन्ने थाहा पाइन्छ । पाटनका मणिकुल, त्रिरत्न, भैषज्यराज एवं सुमङ्गल विहार र काठमाडौंको कोटेश्वरमा अवस्थित अर्को एक विहार गरी यस विहारका पाँच वटा शाखाविहार रहेका छन् । पाटनमा भएका विहारहरूमध्ये यो बही नै सबैभन्दा बढी संख्यामा शाखा विहार (कचा बहाः) भएको विहार हो ।लक (१९८५: २१२) का अनुसार १९८५ मा यस बहीका १३५ सङ्घ सदस्य रहेका थिए र पाटनका विहारका सङ्घहरू मध्ये यो नै सबैभन्दा बढि सदस्य रहेको सङ्घ थियो । शाक्य ब्रह्मचारी भिक्षुहरू मात्र यस संघका सदस्य हुन्छन् । संघले बहीको नित्य पूजा एवं अन्य धार्मिक सामाजिक कार्यहरू सम्पन्न गर्दै आएको छ । संघमा आवद्ध प्रत्येक परिवारलाई एक हप्ताको अन्तरालमा आइतवारको दिन नित्य पूजाको जिम्मेवारी हस्तान्तरण गरिन्छ । नित्य पूजाको जिम्मेवारी पाएका सदस्य बही परिसरभित्रै सुत्नुपर्ने चलन छ । विगतमा बहीको पूजाआजाका लागि राखिएका गुठी जग्गाहरू हाल बहीको मातहतमा नरहेकाले आयस्ताको अभावमा बहीका धेरैजसो पूजाआजाका कर्महरू बन्द भएको अवस्था छ । हाल संघकै सदस्यहरूबाट संकलित रकमबाट ती कार्यहरू संचालन भैआएको छ ।बहीको प्राङ्गणमा तीन वटा चैत्य, एउटा धर्मधातु र भक्तका मूर्तिहरू पनि रहेका छन् । सन् २००७ मा सुरु गरिएको बहीछेँको पूर्वी खण्डको पुनःनिर्माण कार्य हाल बजेट अभावमा अपूर्ण अवस्थामै लथालिङ्ग छाडिएको छ ।

historical_events.event_name: Construction of a Śikharakūṭa caitya and the renovation of shrines
historical_events.event_description: A Śikharakūṭacaityawas constructed and the shrines of Gandhuridevatāand Bārāhi were renovated.

historical_events.event_name: Installation of a statue of Gaṇeśa
historical_events.event_description: The inscription records the installation of a Gaṇeśa statue in the Bahī. The inscription has been lost.
Silver ornaments were offered to Śākyamuni and Vajravārāhī.
The copper portion of the statue of the main deity was gilded.
Religious instruments were offered to theguṭhīto perform the daily rituals of Śākyamuni Buddha and Vajravārāhī.

The inscription informs about the installation ofteliyātiles in the Cikã Bahī courtyard. The inscription is inscribed on the stone surface of the upper part of aCaityain Taḥdhã Bahī (LAL1960).(VajrācāryaVS 2068: 37)

historical_events.event_name: Renovation and beautification of the main deity
historical_events.event_description: Renovation work on the main deity was completed and the copper part of the statue was gilded.
Thebahīcomplex was renovated. A photograph inLocke(1985, 211) shows that construction work was carried out in theBahīcourtyard.
The main shrine(gandhurīdeva-degaḥ) was renovated.
The Ministry of Local Development (Sthānīya Vikāsa Mantrālaya) provided funding for the renovatio of the Bahī.
A newly made statue of Mahākāla was installed.

historical_events.event_name: Buddha Jayanti: Sponsoring of festivals and processions
historical_events.event_description: On the occasion of Buddha Jayanti, Jagatmān Vaidya (also known as Dharmāditya Dharmācārya) sponsored a procession, acūḍākarmaceremony and a feast for thesaṅgha. In addition to this he donated Rs. 100 and a piece of land as an endowment. This seems to be the first attempt to revive the ancient observance of Buddha Jayanti which has somewhat lapsed amongst the Buddhists in Nepal (Locke1985, 212).
The plinth was paved with stone.
The inscription reads 'suvarṇakoṣa dayaku thvate' but the meaning is unclear.
Chatrārohaṇa(a parasol was offered to the main deity).Locke(1985: 212) mentions the offering of a golden finial in reference to the inscription of NS 758 (1638 CE).

The Bahī was renovated. After the performance of ayajña,acaitya-shaped pinnacle was installed on top of thepura(phucā). 9tolāof gold, 15dhārniof copper and wages of 30 [Rupees] was spent on this work.
Various ornaments were offered to Śākyamuni and Vajravārāhi.
The metaltoraṇaover the door of the shrine was donated.
Two lion statues were installed in front of the entrance.
A donation of 5mohars(Rs.2.50) was given by each of the families of thesaṅghato repair the Bahī.
